Article Title: Ground zero of Assam’s flood fury: Village vanishes in an hour; toll rises to 78, over 3L affected
Article Text:
Livelihoods? lost to raging waters

Flood toll rises to 78

, over 3L affected





GUWAHATI: Hiloni Nepali Khuti, a thriving village in Assam's Sivasagar district, along the banks of the Dikhow river, consisting of around 200 Gorkha families, has been wiped out by the devastating floods.Once a hamlet of happy souls, it is now reduced to just a barren stretch of sand and debris.Located barely 500 metres from the Dikhow and 3 km from the Assam-Nagaland border, Hiloni Nepali Khuti's fortunes changed forever on the fateful afternoon of July 19, when the river tore through its settlements and swept away homes and families, after a bout of torrential rain in Nagaland led to a massive increase in its volume.Until that morning, the river was a familiar and friendly sight, but all that changed after it rendered an entire settlement, relying primarily on dairy farming to Nazira and nearby towns, homeless.On that fateful morning, the villagers had gone to collect logs and firewood from the Naga Hills downstream - an annual monsoon ritual. Moments later disaster struck, when the river tore through the village and swept away homes, cattle sheds and nearly 4,000 cattle.Today, with only a handful of livestock, the residents are trying to claw their way back to normalcy, albeit with little hope.All the villagers went to collect the logs and firewood carried by the river from Nagaland hills.We collect those every monsoon. We were very happy. But, we noticed rapid increase in water level and increase in quantity of firewood in the water. Thereafter, the water engulfed the entire village and swept everything without leaving an opportunity for us to save our belongings," Balaram Sharma (38), a resident, said.His family took refuge for two days at an elevated landing in his residence, before they were rescued on the third day. He sent his elderly parents, wife and 3-year-old daughter to Namrup in Dibrugarh. He had 23 cattle, of which 16 were swept away by the floods.Similar to Balaram, Prakash Sharma (35), too, managed to save his family members, but lost 56 of his 60 cattle to the Dikhow's outburst. He saved his four cattle with the help of security forces on July 27, eight days after the floods had hit their village.Assam’s flood death toll rose to 78 on Wednesday after three more bodies — two in Sivasagar and one in Golaghat —were recovered, even as over three lakh people remained affected across seven districts.According to ASDMA, the floods have affected 3,00,031 people in 551 villages under 21 revenue circles. The deluge has also inundated 21,523.08 hectares of cropland.
Article Summary: Hiloni Nepali Khuti, a thriving village in Assam's Sivasagar district, along the banks of the Dikhow river, has been wiped out by the devastating floods. A bout of torrential rain in Nagaland led to a massive increase in the volume of the river. The villagers had gone to collect logs and firewood from the Naga Hills downstream.

Article Title: Here's why many MBBS graduates can't take foreign licensing exams
Article Text:
The directory lists medical schools recognisedby the local govt or the ministry concerned, globally

Thousands of students who have completed MBBS are unable to appear for any foreign licensing examination as the colleges they have graduated from have not initiated the process for an "ECFMG sponsor note" in the World Directory of Medical Schools. This is a formal note on a medical college's listing in the world directory indicating that it meets standards set by Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG).The directory aims to list all medical schools which have been recognised by the local govt or ministry concerned, globally. However, colleges listed here might not have sponsor notes that make their students eligible for ECFMG certification, a credential evaluation agency. Colleges can apply electronically for credential verification only after their first batch of graduates, or roughly five years after the first batch is admitted.Usually, colleges start the process when their first batch starts the 12-month compulsory rotating medical internship. However, many students have discovered after MBBS graduation that their colleges have not got ECFMG sponsor notes. Most students who join colleges don't check whether their college has ECFMG sponsor notes till after graduation when they want to sit for USMLE (United States Medical Licensing Examination), UK's PLAB (Professional and Linguistic Assessments Board) or other licensing exams.Many graduates of Kalpana Chawla Medical College in Karnal, Haryana, discovered that their college did not have ECFMG sponsor notes though it admitted its first batch in 2017. Some at AIIMS have not got ECFMG sponsor notes.In response to an RTI query , National Medical Commission (NMC) stated that "as and when any information or documents to update ECFMG sponsor note in respect of Indian medical colleges is asked by ECFMG, the same is provided to ECFMG immediately after due process and approval of competent authority".NMC's response on June 30 stated the submission of information to ECFMG to update sponsor notes on the world directory list was under process in NMC for several colleges.There was no response from NMC and Union health ministry to TOI's queries on whether it was mandated that all Indian medical colleges must apply to ECFMG sponsor notes on time, and on students' complaints on the issue.
Article Summary: Thousands of students unable to appear for foreign licensing exams as colleges have not initiated process for "ECFMG sponsor note" This is a formal note on a medical college's listing in the world directory indicating that it meets standards set by Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates. Colleges can apply electronically for credential verification only after their first batch of graduates.

NEW DELHI:These are the words of 69-year old Union minister Jitendra SIngh, who was addressing the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Until recently, these words belonged to Instagram comment sections, meme pages, K-pop fan communities and WhatsApp chats. This week, however, they echoed through the halls of Parliament.During the Monsoon session, MPs infused their speeches with Gen Z slang and internet catchphrases while taking on political rivals, discussing governance and framing arguments around issues ranging from education to development.BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj, while defending the Centre's policies, urged the Opposition to "" — a Gen Z phrase meaning to recognise or acknowledge something. "Where Congress created a policy vacuum, Modi clocked it, if I may borrow the language of Gen Z, and created a solution. All the Opposition did was chase political opportunism," she said, explicitly acknowledging that she was borrowing from the vocabulary of younger generations.BJP’s Tejasvi Surya reached for another popular internet expression, calling the Opposition "" — shorthand for "delusional" — suggesting its criticism of the government was detached from reality.Not to be left behind, Congress MP Deepender Hooda, during debate on anti-paper leak in Lok Sabha, slipped in ‘’ and viral internet catchphrase “” in a swipe at Centre. “(Today is my birthday, so please resign cutie pie)," he remarked, giving example of slogans at the recent student protests.Meanwhile, Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Eknath Shinde labelled the Opposition as suffering from "" — the "Fear of Missing Out" — and even described it as "" (Missing in Action), implying that the Opposition was scrambling to remain politically relevant after missing key opportunities.It was an unusual moment.As Hooda put it, the GenZ with Bhagat Singh’s slogan of ‘Inquilab Zindabad’, turned it into ‘Vastaguna huiya’ when they protested against the government.Parliament, traditionally associated with constitutional language, Hindi idioms and literary references, suddenly sounded like an Instagram comment thread.The internet has a way of making words travel across continents, cultures and generations. Many expressions that now dominate Gen Z conversations were born in niche online communities long before they entered mainstream discourse.Unlike many internet expressions, "clock it" has a much older cultural lineage. The phrase traces its roots to African-American and LGBTQ+ ballroom culture in the United States, where "to clock" someone meant to notice, identify or call out something—often a flaw or inconsistency.Popularised through drag culture and shows such as, the expression later migrated to TikTok and Instagram, where Gen Z adopted it to mean "spot the truth" or "call it as it is".The phrase traces its roots to the viral meme "Can I get a Hoya?", in which a teenager shouted the line in an exaggerated tone. In India, content creators gave the meme a local twist by replacing the original phrase with the nonsensical-sounding "Vasteguna Huiya".The humour lay not in the words themselves—they have no literal meaning—but in the confused reactions they elicited. From there, the phrase spread rapidly across Instagram memes, reels and comment sections before making its way into the CJP student protests."Kuchu Puchu" does not have a single, traceable origin like "delulu" or "FOMO". Instead, it evolved organically from baby talk, a simplified, affectionate style of speech used by parents, grandparents and couples across many Indian languages.The phrase is believed to be a playful variation of words like "kuchi kuchi," "guchu puchu," "kuchi poo," and similar rhyming expressions that mimic the sounds babies make. Such reduplicative words are common in Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and several other Indian languages, where they are used as terms of endearment for children, pets or romantic partners.In recent years, "kuchu puchu" was revived and popularised by Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and meme pages, where it took on a new, often sarcastic meaning. Calling someone "kuchu puchu" can imply that they are overly pampered, babied, innocent or treated with excessive affection.Its popularity surged during the CJP-led student protests, where protesters and social media users used "kuchu puchu" satirically to poke fun at political leaders and institutions.Unlike most Gen Z slang, FOMO predates social media. The acronym, standing for "Fear of Missing Out", entered popular vocabulary in the early 2000s as psychologists and marketers described the anxiety people felt when they believed others were enjoying experiences they were not part of.Instagram amplified the phenomenon, turning FOMO into one of the defining emotions of the social media age. Today, the term is used far beyond personal life—to describe everything from investment trends to political strategy.Originally a military abbreviation for "Missing in Action", MIA has been repurposed by internet users to describe people who suddenly disappear from conversations, social media or public life.Perhaps the most recognisable Gen Z word today, "delulu" is a shortened version of "delusional". It first gained popularity within K-pop fandoms, where devoted fans jokingly described unrealistic fantasies—such as believing their favourite idol secretly loved them—as being "delulu".Over time, the term evolved beyond fandom culture to describe anyone perceived as wildly optimistic or disconnected from reality. Today, it has become a staple of political banter, where opponents routinely accuse each other of being "delulu".The timing of Parliament's linguistic makeover is not accidental.The recent protests spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over NEET examination paper leaks were organised as much on Instagram and X as they were on the streets. Protesters used memes, short-form videos, viral hashtags and internet humour to mobilise students and simplify complex issues around examination reforms.For many young Indians, politics is now consumed through Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and meme pages rather than lengthy parliamentary speeches or television debates. Viral clips often carry more influence than hour-long discussions.Taking notice of the same after massive protests, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also advised his Cabinet to engage with the youth on Instagram through reels and interactive sessions. "Young people are just on Instagram. This is a potential segment of citizens that we all need to connect with," he said.India's demographic profile makes this shift even more significant. With one of the world's youngest populations and millions of first-time voters entering the electorate every election cycle, speaking the language of youth has become a political strategy as much as a communication style.Although Gen Z slangs in Parliament may sound dramatic, Parliament has always reflected the language of its times.In the early decades after Independence, speeches frequently quoted verses from the, couplets by poets like Mirza Ghalib, Allama Iqbal. Hindi literary works were seen as a mark of oratorical skill.Long before MPs began saying "delulu" or "clock it", Parliament had embraced the language of popular culture. Bollywood dialogues have long been used to simplify political arguments, inject humour and produce memorable sound bites.Rahul Gandhi's dig at GST by calling it "Gabbar Singh Tax" transformed a complex debate on GST into a phrase instantly understood across India, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi invoked the character "Mausi" from the Sholay to mock the Congress party during his address in Parliament on July 2, 2024. He teased the opposition over their electoral defeat by mimicking a dialogue: "" (Oh Mausi, we have lost for the third time too, but it's a moral victory, right?).In another instance, BJP MP Kangana Ranaut brought DDLJ’s iconic dialogue ‘’ to life while addressing women’s reservation bill in Lok Sabha.Cricket metaphors soon followed, with terms like "hitting a six", "playing on the back foot" or being "clean bowled" by the Opposition. Finance ministers have described Budgets as "innings", while election victories and defeats have routinely been framed as cricket matches.In many ways, Gen Z slang is simply the latest chapter in this evolution. Parliament has never existed in a linguistic vacuum; it has always absorbed the language spoken beyond its walls.Every generation believes the next one's vocabulary sounds strange.Words like "cool", "awesome", "dude" and "LOL" were once dismissed as youthful fads before becoming mainstream. Today's internet lexicon follows the same trajectory.Many Gen Z expressions have travelled remarkable distances—from Korean pop fandoms to American drag culture, from gaming communities to TikTok trends—before landing in Indian political discourse. Their journey illustrates how digital platforms have accelerated the movement of language across borders and cultures.Not every slang term will survive. Internet vocabulary evolves at dizzying speed, with new words replacing old ones every few months. But some expressions inevitably escape their online origins to become part of everyday speech.When lawmakers adopt them, it signals that these words have crossed into the mainstream.When Bansuri Swaraj paused to say, "if I may borrow the language of Gen Z", she acknowledged something larger than a passing linguistic trend.Politics is no longer communicated solely through ideological speeches or parliamentary rhetoric. It increasingly competes in the same digital ecosystem as influencers, meme pages and viral videos, where relatability often matters as much as reasoned argument.Whether that makes parliamentary debate more accessible or more performative remains open to debate. But one thing is clear: as India's politics becomes increasingly digital, the House is learning to speak not just to Gen Z, but increasingly like Gen Z.
Article Summary: Parliament, traditionally associated with constitutional language, Hindi idioms and literary references, suddenly sounded like an Instagram comment thread. MPs infused their speeches with Gen Z slang and internet catchphrases while taking on political rivals, discussing governance and framing arguments around issues ranging from education to development.

Article Title: 'Embarrassing': Ex-Olympian and hockey captain slams India's blue jersey being replaced by saffron
Article Text:
India's iconic blue jersey being replaced by saffron (Screengrab)

Viren Rasquinha criticised Hockey India’s decision to replace the team’s iconic blue jersey with saffron

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India set to begin World Cup campaign

NEW DELHI: Former India hockey captain and Olympian Viren Rasquinha has criticised Hockey India’s decision to replace the team's traditional blue jersey with a saffron one ahead of the 2026 Hockey World Cup.Expressing his disappointment on X (formerly Twitter), he wrote, "I must say that @TheHockeyIndia has done many good things for (hockey emotes). But this is embarrassing. The legacy & identity of the Indian team has always been BLUE. I wore the Blue jersey with pride for many years. Fans want to see our Indian team in blue. What is the logic of orange?"Hockey India has unveiled new kits for both the men's and women's teams before the 2026 Hockey World Cup, with saffron replacing blue as the main colour.The jersey also features mandala-inspired designs, tricolour detailing and blue accents. Explaining the change, Hockey India said, "Symbolises courage, sacrifice & victory. Inspired by the Indian national flag and the rising sun, it reflects new beginnings."Further explaining the rationale behind questioning the decision, he made another post on X, adding, "I’m seeing many unnecessary political comments on this. I don’t want to get into any of that. My simple & humble point is on pride, identity & legacy. (India) is to (hockey) what Argentina is to Football. Will we ever see Argentina wearing Orange and White stripes as their 1st jersey?"The 2026 Hockey World Cup will be held in the Netherlands and Belgium from August 14 to 30, with the men's and women's tournaments taking place together for the first time.The Indian men's team, placed in Group D, will face Wales, England and Pakistan in the group stage.The women's team, also in Group D, will begin against China before taking on South Africa and England. India’s men have won the Hockey World Cup once, in 1975, while the women’s best finish was fourth place in 1974.
Article Summary: Hockey India has unveiled new kits for both the men's and women's teams before the 2026 Hockey World Cup. Former India hockey captain and Olympian Viren Rasquinha has criticised Hockey India’s decision to replace the team's traditional blue jersey with a saffron one.

Article Title: Candace Owens drops unseen Charlie Kirk video, Alex Jones claims assassination story is ‘100% dead’
Article Text:
Candace Owens drops unseen Charlie Kirk video, Alex Jones claims assassination story is ‘100% dead’ (Image via Getty)

Alex Jones says Candace Owens’ video raises fresh questions about Tyler Robinson

What Candace Owens claimed after releasing the Charlie Kirk rooftop footage

Charlie Kirk’s 2025 assassination is back in the spotlight after conservative commentator Candace Owens released what she said was never-before-seen rooftop footage of the suspected gunman. Owens argued that the man in the video does not match Tyler Robinson, who was arrested after the shooting and accused by authorities of carrying out the attack. Soon after the footage was released, Alex Jones publicly backed her claims, saying the “official narrative” had “collapsed.” The video has now added fresh attention to a case that is still moving through the courts. A judge has not yet decided whether Robinson will stand trial.After Candace Owens shared the rooftop footage on July 28, Alex Jones reposted it and strongly supported her claims. He argued that the clip appeared to be “raw and unedited” and questioned whether it matched the version of events presented by investigators.Jones wrote:“The Official Charlie Kirk assassination story is now 100% dead! Candace Owens just dropped powerful never before seen surveillance video of the Losee Center rooftop.The video Owens released appears to be raw and unedited! This is the same footage that the court will not let the public see, that we are meant to believe is Tyler Robinson assassinating Charlie Kirk.”He then compared the person seen in the video with Robinson and claimed they did not appear to be the same individual.“The individual does not look like Tyler Robinson. The rifle is never pulled from his pants. The person in the footage has no limp. Nowhere do we see the shooter assembling the gun on the roof as we were told. No recoil is seen. He performs military maneuvers with precision as well as signaling before opening fire. The official narrative just COLLAPSED…”Earlier this month, surveillance footage shown during Robinson’s preliminary hearing appeared to show a man walking across the Utah Valley University campus with what prosecutors described as a limp before the shooting.Candace Owens has repeatedly questioned whether Tyler Robinson was responsible for Charlie Kirk’s killing. She raised similar doubts in a previous interview with CNN journalist Elle Reeve and repeated those claims during the latest episode of her podcast, where she played the newly released video.While explaining the footage, Owens said the man on the rooftop carried out what she described as a military-style movement.“Now what happens next is exactly as my source stipulated. Now the rooftop guy begins a tactical crawl that is actually known in the military as a lateral crawl. Let’s watch that…I actually want to show you a side-by-side so you can actually see a real military man do that… that general action right there is known as a lateral crawl.”She also pointed to another moment in the clip that she believed deserved attention.“He comes running onto the rooftop. What we know definitively is he gets down into what is known as a lateral military crawl. Begins that crawl over to the right first and then to the left we see a quick flash. We are not sure what that flash is. Um actually this looks like, oh, I’m not going to read into it. There’s that throw forward. I say fold forward. You can say throw forward, but that’s definitely something being flung forward, getting into position. ”Authorities have continued to identify Tyler Robinson as the accused in the case. As of now, the court has not decided whether he will face trial.
Article Summary: Conservative commentator Candace Owens released what she said was never-before- seen rooftop footage of the suspected gunman. Owens argued that the man in the video does not match Tyler Robinson, who was arrested after the shooting and accused by authorities of carrying out the attack. Alex Jones publicly backed her claims, saying the “official narrative” had “collapsed.”

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “Serbian history tells that family is the most important thing.” - How Novak Djokovic turned poverty and family sacrifice into tennis greatness
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “Serbian history tells that family is the most important thing.” - How Novak Djokovic turned poverty, and family sacrifice into tennis greatness (Image via Getty)

How did Novak Djokovic survive war and still keep chasing his tennis dream?

How did Novak Djokovic’s parents sacrifice everything for his career?

Why did Novak Djokovic publicly defend his family during controversy?

Why does Novak Djokovic’s life story continue to inspire people around the world?

Before Novak Djokovic became the only player to win 24 Grand Slam singles titles and an Olympic gold medal, he was a young boy growing up in one of the hardest times in Serbia’s history. At just 12 years old, he spent nights hiding from air raids during the 1999 NATO bombing of Belgrade. At the same time, his parents were doing everything they could to keep his tennis dream alive, even when they had almost nothing. Years later, Djokovic has often said that those difficult days shaped the person and champion he became, giving him the strength that carried him to the top of world tennis.In 1999, life changed overnight for the Djokovic family. During the NATO bombing campaign, they spent 78 straight nights waking up around 2 or 3 a.m. and taking shelter in the basement of Novak’s grandfather’s apartment as bombs fell across Belgrade.Even in those frightening days, Djokovic did not stop playing tennis. He trained whenever he could, sometimes on damaged courts surrounded by bomb craters. Looking back on those days, he said they changed the way he looked at life and competition.“It’s the fear of the unknown. Not knowing if the next bomb is going to hit your head… We were waking up every single night more or less at two, three a.m.for two and a half months. But it made us tougher. It made us more hungry, more hungry for the success.”Those experiences became the foundation of the mental strength that many fans admire in his game today.War was only one challenge. Money was another.Tennis was an expensive sport, and Djokovic’s parents, Srdjan and Dijana, did not have the resources to support a professional tennis career. They ran a small pancake and pizza shop in the mountains and borrowed money from high-interest lenders to pay for coaching, equipment and travel.His mother, Dijana, has spoken about days when there was no money left in the family’s bank account. His father, Srdjan, once placed the family’s last 10-Deutsche Mark note on the table and told everyone that it was all they had.Djokovic has never forgotten those sacrifices.“Serbian history tells that family is the most important thing and you have to stick with the family. My parents went through a lot of hardships, financially, emotionally, every way… To see my parents struggle so much just so I could play tennis, it gave me a responsibility and a drive that never left me.”He has often said that his parents’ struggles became one of the biggest reasons he pushed himself to succeed.As Djokovic became one of the biggest names in tennis, his family also found themselves in the spotlight. During different controversies over the years, he repeatedly stood by them while making it clear where they stood on violence and war.Speaking about his family’s past, Djokovic said their own experiences left no room for supporting conflict.“My father, my whole family, and myself, have been through several wars during the ’90s. As my father put in a statement, we are against the war, we never will support any violence or any war. We know how devastating that is for the family, for people in any country that is going through the war.”His comments reflected the lessons his family carried from living through years of conflict.Today, millions know Djokovic for breaking records and winning some of the biggest matches in tennis history. But the story behind those victories began long before the trophies.His childhood was filled with fear, financial struggles and uncertainty. Yet, instead of giving up, his family stayed together and kept believing that a better future was possible.That journey explains why Djokovic often speaks about family, resilience and gratitude. His success was not built only on talent. It also came from the sacrifices made by his parents and the determination he developed while growing up in one of the toughest periods of his country’s history.For many people, that part of his story is just as inspiring as the records he has set on the tennis court.
Article Summary: Novak Djokovic is the only player to win 24 Grand Slam singles titles and an Olympic gold medal. His success was not built on talent, but on the sacrifices made by his parents. At just 12 years old, he spent nights hiding from air raids during the 1999 NATO bombing of Belgrade.

Article Title: 'Clicky Ponting' cheating row: Saltburn Cricket Club suspends player, calls the incident 'very distressing'
Article Text:
Saltburn Cricket Club suspends player over cheating allegations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Saltburn Cricket Club have suspended a player, humorously called "Clicky Ponting", after he was accused of cheating during a local league match by clicking his fingers to make it sound like the batter had edged the ball.The incident, which happened during Saltburn’s second XI win over Norton, went viral on social media after video footage appeared to show the fielder making the sound just before the wicketkeeper completed the catch.The umpire gave the batter out, sparking widespread criticism online.Responding to the controversy, Saltburn Cricket Club, an English outfit, said they were taking the allegations seriously and had suspended the player while an investigation is underway.In a statement, the club said, “We are treating this allegation with the utmost seriousness and, as a family-centric club, we are fully cooperating with the NYS League’s investigation.”The statement added, “The player at the centre of the complaint has been suspended and will not play again for the club this season or in the foreseeable future, pending the outcome of this investigation.”Saltburn have also withdrawn from their second-team cup match against Marton as the investigation continues.Club officials have already spoken with league representatives and said the situation has been difficult for everyone involved.They added, “This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club entirely run by volunteers.”The viral clip has now been viewed more than 7.5 million times on X, with several well-known figures criticising the alleged act.
Article Summary: Saltburn Cricket Club have suspended a player over cheating allegations. The player was accused of clicking his fingers to make it sound like the batter had edged the ball. The incident happened during Saltburn’s second XI win over Norton. The viral clip has now been viewed more than 7.5 million times on X.

Authorities say the confrontation escalated quickly and led to an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon charge.According to the arrest report by CBS Sports, the incident happened on a Miami Beach bus near Abbott Avenue and Island Creek Drive.According to the police, Demetrious Byrd caused a disturbance on the bus. Another passenger tried to calm him down, but the situation worsened. Investigators allege Byrd removed a silver multi-tool from his pocket, opened the blade, and approached the passenger.The arrest report says Byrd asked, “Who wants to die?” during the confrontation. Kelsey Plum is entering the final months of a one-year, $999,999 contract with the 10-17 Los Angeles Sparks, and sources tell The Athletic she does not plan to re-sign this winter. With the Aug. 2 trade deadline four days out, Golden State, Washington and Phoenix have all surfaced as speculative destinations, though the Sparks front office, run on an interim basis since firing GM Raegan Pebley this month, has yet to open real trade talks.The Kelsey Plum trade rumors are building as the Sparks sit 10-17 and five games back of the final playoff spot after the All-Star break, the longest active postseason drought in the league dating to 2020. Plum, 31, signed her one-year deal with Los Angeles this season, but sources tell The Athletic she has no intention of returning as a free agent.That puts the Sparks front office, now steered on an interim basis by assistant GMs Zach Knowlton and Nate Nielsen after the midseason firing of Raegan Pebley, in a bind. Move Plum before Sunday's deadline or risk losing her in free agency for nothing.The Sparks doubled down on winning this offseason, re-signing Plum and Dearica Hamby, adding Nneka Ogwumike and Erica Wheeler, and trading Rickea Jackson for Ariel Atkins.None of it has worked. Plum got off to a career-best start before injuries limited her to 12 games, and she hasn't played since June 21, missing this year's All-Star Game. Cameron Brink, the former No. 2 pick, has managed just 19 games. The defense that was supposed to improve with Ogwumike and Atkins in the fold instead ranks 14th in the league at a 113 defensive rating.With Plum and Ogwumike both facing free agency this winter, the front office has one asset it controls right now: the ability to trade Plum instead of letting her walk. The one bright spot is the Sparks' own 2027 first-round pick, which figures to land in a strong lottery class regardless of what happens with Plum.Three teams stand out as plausible fits. Golden State needs scoring above all else. Before her injury, Plum averaged a career-high 23.9 points on 52.7/38.3/80.6 shooting splits, a mark that would rank sixth all-time for a single season if she qualified, and the Valkyries don't have a single player averaging 15 points a game despite owning the league's best defense at a 100.9 rating.Since six of the last ten champions ranked first in offensive rating. The problem is cost: Golden State has no cap space and won't trade Gabby Williams, so a deal likely needs two players plus draft compensation, and the Valkyries would want assurance Plum re-signs before paying that price.Washington offers a cleaner financial path, with nearly $2 million in cap space and a backcourt that badly needs her, since Georgia Amoore is still rounding into form after an ACL tear and Alicia Florez has struggled worse.The Mystics also control a possible top-three pick via a Chicago swap and Chicago's outright 2028 first, though whether Plum wants to commit long-term to Washington, after spending nearly her entire career on the West Coast, is unresolved. Phoenix is the longest shot.The Mercury are five and a half games behind Washington for the eighth seed and on pace to miss the playoffs for the first time since 2008 the season after a Finals trip, and The Athletic reports their earlier talks around Alyssa Thomas have gone cold. Plum wouldn't push Phoenix into the race with 16 games left, but the appeal would be getting her in the building ahead of a long-term deal, even though Phoenix's $850,000 in cap space comes with little young talent to meet a Sparks asking price built around multiple firsts.The Athletic reports that Plum's camp does not expect her back in Los Angeles, based on team sources who spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't cleared to discuss it publicly. Plum and her agent, Zack Miller of WME Basketball, declined to comment. Multiple team executives around the league say the Sparks haven't engaged in meaningful trade conversations involving Plum despite the looming deadline.Sparks coach Lynne Roberts addressed the uncertainty this week without naming names. "We're not where we want to be right now," she said, adding that the front office is evaluating everything heading into Sunday.The broader market is unusually active this year. Roster rules in the new collective bargaining agreement, including a minimum salary cap exception and the ability to carry seven protected veteran contracts instead of six, have front offices more willing to move. Wings GM Curt Miller captured that mindset, saying teams "can't be afraid to make bold moves when you have a championship opportunity."Plum signed her current one-year, $999,999 deal with the Sparks for the 2026 season. Across 12 games before her injury, she posted career-high averages of 23.9 points, 2.2 rebounds, 6.4 assists and 1.2 steals a game.The Aug. 2 deadline is now the deciding moment. Los Angeles either moves Plum this weekend or gambles on convincing her to stay through an offseason the franchise has repeatedly failed to win.
Article Summary: Kelsey Plum is entering the final months of a one-year, $999,999 contract with the 10-17 Los Angeles Sparks. Sources tell The Athletic she does not plan to re- sign this winter. Golden State Valkyries, Washington Mystics, Phoenix Mercury have all surfaced as speculative destinations.

NEW DELHI: Former India captain Ajinkya Rahane has announced his retirement from international cricket.Rahane shared the news through a post on Instagram, where he uploaded a video message with the caption: "Cap 278 signing off"."Thank you for all the love and support over the years. Forever grateful," Rahane wrote in his post."The reality of life is that everything has a beginning and everything has an end. When the time comes, you simply have to respect it and move forward. I have always relied on timing in my batting and have always understood its importance," Rahane said."Today, I feel the timing is right for me to move on and announce my retirement from international cricket and all formats. From those early days, travelling as a young boy just to practice, I gave this game everything I had. Every single day, every innings, every opportunity I got to bat, the dream was always to wear the India cap," he added."I lived by one simple rule. Always put my country and my team ahead of myself. I played this game with complete honesty and I have always believed that if your intent is right, the game will always take care of you," the veteran cricketer said."Since the time I made my debut as a first-class cricketer, Indian cricket has grown tremendously and I feel so proud to have been a part of it over the last 20 years. While my chapter as an Indian cricketer comes to an end, my journey with the game doesn't. I look forward to helping the next generation, sharing the values this sport has taught me and giving back to the game that has given me everything," he said.Rahane also thanked the BCCI, Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA), his teammates, coaches, IPL franchises, family, friends and fans for their support throughout his career."And a very special thank you to all the cricket fans who supported me through every high and low. Ajinkya means unbeatable, but cricket has shown me defeat many times. As cricketers, we fail more often than we succeed. My team has lost matches. I have made mistakes, but there is one place where I was never defeated. And that was in your hearts. Thank you for your love, your faith and your support. Cap number 278, signing off," Rahane concludedThe 36-year-old represented India in all three formats during his international career. He played 85 Test matches, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is.The right-handed batter scored 5,077 runs in Tests at 38.46 with 12 centuries and 26 fifties, while in 90 ODIs, he made 2,962 runs at 35.26 including three tons and 24 fifties. In 20 T20Is, Rahane made 375 runs.Rahane's biggest moment came in 2021 when he famously stood in for regular skipper Virat Kohli as a heavily depleted India defeated Australia in their own backyard 2-1.
Article Summary: Former India captain Ajinkya Rahane has announced his retirement from international cricket. The 36-year-old represented India in all three formats during his international career. He played 85 Test matches, 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is. Rahane scored 5,077 runs in Tests at 38.46 with 12 centuries and 26 fifties.

Why this could be one of his toughest Commonwealth Games competitions

NEW DELHI: Neeraj Chopra walks into the Commonwealth Games 2026 as India’s biggest athletics hope, but this may be far from a routine title defence.The Olympic champion and former world champion is returning to the Games after an eight-year gap, and the men’s javelin field in Glasgow is significantly stronger than the one he conquered in Gold Coast in 2018.Back then, Neeraj won gold with an 86.47m throw and looked a class apart. This time, he enters Scotstoun Stadium with questions around form, fitness and the depth of the competition. He missed Birmingham 2022 due to injury, and his 2026 season only began recently after recovering from a back problem.His first outing of the year at the Doha Diamond League showed both promise and rust. Neeraj produced a best throw of 85.69m, briefly moved into medal contention, but eventually finished fourth after two foul throws.For an athlete whose standards are now measured in 88m-plus and 90m territory, Doha suggested he is not yet at his absolute peak.The most obvious threat is Pakistan’s Arshad Nadeem. The rivalry between Neeraj and Arshad has become one of the defining stories in world athletics. Arshad owns a personal best of 92.97m, one of the greatest throws in history. His listed season best is only 78.47m, but that number is misleading because he has competed sparingly and has repeatedly shown he can produce huge throws in major championships.Grenada’s Anderson Peters is arguably the most dangerous athlete in the field on current form. The two-time world champion has a personal best of 93.07m and a season best of 86.38m, slightly better than Neeraj’s. Peters is known for his ability to throw consistently over 85m, which is often enough to stay in medal contention throughout a competition.Then there is Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, the emerging force of the field. At just 23, he arrives with a personal and season best of 92.62m, making him statistically one of the biggest threats to gold. Unlike some rivals whose best marks came years ago, Rumesh has already crossed 92m this season.India also has Rohit Yadav, who has thrown 87.05m, while experienced names such as Keshorn Walcott (90.16m PB) and Julius Yego (92.72m PB) add further quality to the competition.The biggest challenge for Neeraj is not just one rival; it is the number of athletes capable of throwing beyond 85m. In 2018, he was clearly ahead of the field. In Glasgow, at least five athletes have personal bests above 90m, and several have season marks within touching distance of his own.Another factor is timing. Neeraj is still building rhythm after a back injury, and javelin is an event where technical sharpness matters as much as physical strength. A small loss of timing at release can cost two or three metres, which could be the difference between gold and bronze in a field this deep.The format also adds pressure. Qualification is on Thursday, with the final in the early hours of August 1 (IST). Athletes must manage recovery, rhythm and conditions across two rounds, and one poor series can end a medal challenge quickly.Neeraj remains the favourite because of his championship temperament. He has repeatedly delivered under pressure at the Olympics, World Championships and Asian Games. But unlike Gold Coast 2018, this will not be a competition he can win by reputation alone.If he throws 88m or more, a second Commonwealth gold is very likely. If he stays around the 85-86m range seen in Doha, Glasgow could turn into one of the most competitive and unpredictable javelin finals of his career.
Article Summary: Olympic champion and former world champion is returning to the Games after an eight-year gap. His first outing of the year at the Doha Diamond League showed both promise and rust. The most obvious threat is Pakistan’s Arshad Nadeem, who owns a personal best of 92.97m.

NEW DELHI: Teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has continued his dream start to international cricket, making a stunning 230-place leap in the latest ICC Men's T20I Batting Rankings after starring in India's 3-0 series sweep over Zimbabwe.The 15-year-old's meteoric rise headlines the latest rankings update, while Ishan Kishan tightened his grip on the world No. 1 spot after registering the third-highest batting rating in T20I history during the Harare series.Sooryavanshi announced himself on the international stage with a memorable series against Zimbabwe, scoring 151 runs in three matches at an average of 50.33. His performances, which included two half-centuries, earned him the Player of the Series award and a remarkable rise of 230 places in the ICC rankings.The teenage opener is now ranked 48th among T20I batters with 536 rating points, marking a new career-best ranking.While he still trails India's senior stars, the leap underlines the rapid impact he has made in international cricket and reinforces his status as one of the game's brightest young talents.At the top of the batting rankings, Ishan Kishan retained his position as the world's No. 1 T20I batter with 910 rating points, comfortably ahead of Pakistan's Sahibzada Farhan, who is second with 848 points.Kishan had briefly reached a career-high 916 rating points after his brilliant 81-run knock in the second T20I against Zimbabwe. That tally is the third-highest batting rating ever recorded in T20I cricket, behind only Abhishek Sharma (931) and England's Dawid Malan (919).Although his rating dipped slightly after the final match, Kishan's career-best figure of 916 remains higher than the peak ratings achieved by Indian greats Suryakumar Yadav (912) and Virat Kohli (909).As the ICC noted, "Sooryavanshi's rating of 536 points is well adrift of his more experienced teammates, but Kishan can now boast of having a better career batter rating than more accomplished Indian players like Suryakumar Yadav (912) and Virat Kohli (909)."India enjoyed a productive week across the T20I rankings.Tilak Varma climbed two places to sixth among batters, while captain Shreyas Iyer gained seven spots to 24th after the Zimbabwe series.Among bowlers, Ravi Bishnoi surged 31 places to 41st following his three wickets in the series. Varun Chakravarthy, who missed the tour through injury, slipped three places but remained inside the top 10.Zimbabwe also had reason to celebrate despite the series defeat. Ryan Burl climbed six places to joint 85th among T20I batters, while fast bowler Blessing Muzarabani rose 10 spots to 26th in the bowling rankings.

Cricket icon Sachin Tendulkar paid a heartfelt tribute to his late mentor, Ramakant Achrekar, on the occasion of Guru Purnima, expressing gratitude for the coach who laid the foundation of his legendary career. The batting great shared pictures from his visit to Achrekar's memorial at Mumbai's Shivaji Park and reflected on the invaluable lessons his coach imparted, both on and off the field.In an emotional message posted on social media, Tendulkar wrote:"Standing here today, I realised something. Happy Guru Purnima, Achrekar Sir."Achrekar was instrumental in nurturing Tendulkar's talent during his formative years at the famous Shivaji Park. Known for his strict discipline and emphasis on hard work, the veteran coach played a crucial role in developing Tendulkar's technique, temperament, and dedication, qualities that later defined one of the greatest careers in cricket history. Over the years, Tendulkar has repeatedly acknowledged Achrekar's influence, often crediting him for preparing him to handle the pressures of international cricket from a young age.A memorial honouring Ramakant Achrekar was unveiled at Shivaji Park in 2024, celebrating his immense contribution to Indian cricket. Tendulkar attended the unveiling ceremony, paying tribute to the man widely regarded as one of the country's most influential cricket coaches.Sachin Tendulkar concluded his legendary 24-year international cricketing career as the highest run-scorer and century-maker in the history of international cricket. Making his international debut for India at the tender age of 16 in 1989, he played continuously until his emotional farewell at his home ground in Mumbai in November 2013. He widely represents the gold standard of modern batting, finishing with 34,357 international runs and an unprecedented 100 international centuries.
Article Summary: Sachin Tendulkar visited Ramakant Achrekar's memorial at Shivaji Park. The batsman paid tribute to his late mentor on the occasion of Guru Purnima. Achreker was regarded as one of India's most influential cricket coaches. A memorial will be unveiled at the Mumbai ground in 2024.

Why Russell Westbrook still has more in his sleeves

Russell Westbrook's free agency has stalled to the point where retirement is now part of the conversation. According to NBA reporter Evan Sidery, the nine-time All-Star is generating little to no interest from teams around the league, raising the possibility he opens the 2026-27 season without a contract for the first time in his career.Westbrook is coming off his 18th NBA season, one he spent starting for a rebuilding Sacramento Kings team. At 37, with seven franchises already on his resume, the soon-to-be Hall of Famer is staring down an ending nobody expected to arrive quietly.Westbrook entered the offseason as an unrestricted free agent after wrapping up his lone season in Sacramento, his seventh NBA stop. Despite his age, he stayed a fixture in the Kings' rotation, appearing in 64 games and starting 58 of them.He averaged 15.2 points, 6.7 assists, 5.4 rebounds and 1.3 steals in 28.9 minutes per game, shooting 42.7% from the field and 33.8% from three, and recorded six triple-doubles along the way. Those numbers would normally keep a veteran point guard employed without much drama.Instead, Sidery's reporting suggests the market has gone cold. An opening-night roster spot is no longer a given, a stark shift for a player who spent over a decade as one of the league's most durable stars.Nothing suggests Westbrook has decided to walk away, but the silence around him says plenty. He built his reputation with the Oklahoma City Thunder, who drafted him fourth overall in 2008 and rode his explosiveness to the 2012 NBA Finals alongside Kevin Durant and James Harden.That run ended with a 2019 trade to the Houston Rockets. From there, Westbrook bounced through the Washington Wizards, a short and turbulent stint with the Los Angeles Lakers alongside LeBron James and Anthony Davis, a trade to the Utah Jazz, a buyout, a run with the LA Clippers, a season in Denver, and finally Sacramento.That much movement in six seasons already told the story of a player whose role kept shrinking around the league. Now the roster spot itself is in question.Retirement talk aside, there's a case that Westbrook still has real value if a team is willing to use him correctly. The Washington Wizards, pushing for their first playoff push in six seasons after adding Deandre Ayton, Khris Middleton, Trae Young and Anthony Davis, are reportedly still hunting for a veteran backup point guard to pair with Bub Carrington.Westbrook's shooting has always been the weak spot in his game, a career 30.8% from three, but surrounding him with shooters like Tre Johnson, Kyshawn George and Carrington could mask that flaw while letting him run the second unit. He posted 3.7 rim assists per 100 possessions last season, ranking in the 73rd percentile, evidence he can still set up teammates at the basket even without the explosiveness of his prime.Miami has also come up as a landing spot. The New York Post reported Westbrook "is a candidate to join the Heat" should LeBron James sign elsewhere. Westbrook and James spent 18 months together on the Lakers before that pairing ended in a trade, largely because both players wanted the ball in their hands. A bench role in Miami, rather than a marquee starting job, may suit him better at this stage.Given that Westbrook signed for the veteran minimum of $3.6 million in Sacramento last season, cost shouldn't be the obstacle keeping him unsigned.
Article Summary: Russell Westbrook's free agency has stalled to the point where retirement is now part of the conversation. According to NBA reporter Evan Sidery, the nine-time All-Star is generating little to no interest from teams. At 37, with seven franchises already on his resume, the soon-to-be Hall of Famer is staring down an ending nobody expected to arrive quietly.

Article Title: Getting 'carried away' again? Musk's million-dollar plan to rescue Trump in mid-elections
Article Text:
Musk’s massive push

‘Got carried away’ in 2024

Days after Elon Musk admitted that he “got carried away” during Donald Trump’s 2024 election campaign, he is once again stepping into the US political arena with a major push to help Republicans win the 2026 midterm elections. The tech billionaire is reviving his political action committee, America PAC, which played a key role in then-presidential candidate Donald Trump’s 2024 campaign.During the 2024 presidential elections, America PAC spent more than $260 million to help Trump secure a win. This time, the group will focus on increasing Republican voter turnout through door-to-door campaigns, digital advertisements and direct mail.Sources familiar with the plans told Axios that the group will target conservative voters, including those who usually do not vote in non-presidential elections.Though the amount the tech mogul plans to spend has not been revealed yet, it is expected to be large considering his spending during the 2024 election.Musk’s donations through America PAC in 2024 made him the biggest individual political donor in a single US election cycle.The group has said that it knocked on more than 10 million doors across more than six swing states during the campaign.For the 2026 midterms, America PAC will work with other Republican groups.By focusing on voter turnout, Musk’s group will allow other Republican organisations to spend more time and money on television advertisements.The campaign will be led by Musk’s top political adviser, Chris Young.“America PAC was an essential partner for our historic GOTV operation in 2024, and their return for 2026 is a huge boost for Republicans across the country,” James Blair, President Trump's senior political adviser, told Axios.“We will again outsmart our opponents and ruthlessly execute our mission for the GOP between now and Election Day,” Blair added.Musk’s return comes at a time when Republicans have a strong financial advantage over Democrats before the November 3 elections. Republican super PACs and committees have a more than $300 million advantage over Democratic groups and $400 million available in Trump’s MAGA Inc. super PAC.The Republican Party hopes this financial strength will help it overcome concerns around Trump’s low approval ratings, especially on the economy and the Iran war.These concerns have created challenges for Republicans as they try to maintain control of the House and possibly the Senate.Musk has been in talks with Trump’s team about how he can support the Republican campaign.“The president's political team and the rest of the GOP apparatus have built a top-notch operation that will put Republicans in a strong position to buck history and retain control of Congress this fall, and we're excited to again be part of the team,” America PAC spokesperson Andrew Romeo told Axios.Musk’s return to political activity comes days after he admitted that he became too involved in politics during his close relationship with Trump. In an interview with The Economist, the entrepreneur said that he should have spent more time running his companies instead of leading the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).DOGE was a government cost-cutting initiative that oversaw spending cuts and layoffs across government departments. Talking about his political involvement, Musk said, “I got carried away, frankly.”Musk had supported Trump’s 2024 campaign with around $200 million before becoming the head of DOGE.He later admitted that he could have focused more on his businesses. Earlier, during a podcast appearance in December, he had said, “I think instead of doing DOGE, I would have basically worked on my companies,” he had said.Musk’s relationship with Trump became strained after his four-month role leading DOGE. Musk criticised the large spending in Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” and even suggested creating a third party to challenge Republicans.However, his relationship with Trump improved over the following year. By the end of 2025, Musk was again contributing to Republican campaigns.He also donated $10 million to Kentucky GOP Senate candidate Nate Morris, who later left the race to take a job in the Trump administration.
Article Summary: The tech billionaire is reviving his political action committee, America PAC. The group played a key role in then-presidential candidate Donald Trump’s 2024 campaign. America PAC spent more than $260 million to help Trump secure a win. This time, the group will focus on increasing Republican voter turnout through door-to-door campaigns and digital advertisements.

Article Title: Career turning point: “I didn't score a point the entire summer. My father hugged me and said, ‘We're gonna love you if.." How Kobe Bryant turned heartbreak into NBA greatness
Article Text:
A young Kobe Bryant's scoreless summer league became the turning point that fueled his relentless work ethic and eventually shaped the legendary Mamba Mentality.(Getty)

How did one difficult summer change Kobe Bryant 's career forever?

How did that setback become the foundation of the Mamba Mentality for Kobe Bryant?



Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Before Kobe Bryant became the face of the Los Angeles Lakers and one of the greatest players in NBA history, he experienced a moment that could have ended his dream before it truly began. Fans know Bryant for his unmatched competitiveness and the tough mindset that later became known as the Mamba Mentality. But before any of that, he was just a simple boy trying to find his place after returning to the US from Italy, where his family had spent seven years during his father Joe Bryant's professional basketball career.The move back to America was exciting, but it also came with an unexpected reality check. Kobe had grown up around basketball and loved the game, yet the level of competition in the United States was unlike anything he had experienced before. A summer league that was supposed to mark the beginning of his basketball journey instead became one of the most painful moments of his childhood. Cut to now, that disappointing summer did far more than test his confidence. It changed the way he approached basketball and laid the foundation for one of the greatest careers the sport has ever seen.Adjusting to American basketball was far from easy. Although Kobe Bryant had developed strong fundamentals while growing up in Italy, he suddenly found himself playing against some of the best young players in the country.The speed, physicality and confidence of his opponents exposed just how much work he still had to do.Nothing seemed to go right. Game after game, Kobe Bryant struggled to make an impact. By the time the summer league ended, he had failed to score a single point. For a teenager who dreamed of following his father's path to the NBA, the experience was heartbreaking.Years later, Bryant looked back on that summer during an interview with Charlie Rose and did not hide how difficult it had been. He recalled, "I'm back in America in the summertime and I'm playing in the summer league. I didn't score a point the entire summer. Not one point, not a free throw, not a layup, not a steal, nothing. Zero points the whole summer."For many young athletes, an experience like that would have been enough to walk away from the sport. Bryant, however, received something much more valuable than criticism after the season ended.As he walked off the court disappointed, his father came over, hugged him and reminded him that basketball would never define his worth. Joe Bryant told him, "Son, don't worry about it. We're gonna love you if you score zero or 50."Those emotional lines stayed with Kobe for the rest of his life. He later remembered thinking only one thing."Thank you."That simple conversation changed Bryant's outlook. Instead of seeing the scoreless summer as proof that he was not good enough, he began treating it as a starting point. The disappointment showed him where he stood, but it also showed him how much room he had to improve.Bryant became obsessed with getting better. He spent countless hours practicing, working on his footwork and sharpening every part of his game.Around the same time, Bryant also found inspiration in Michael Jordan 's story. Learning that his childhood hero had faced setbacks before becoming an NBA star helped him understand that failure was not something to fear. What mattered was how an athlete responded after it.By the time Bryant entered Lower Merion High School, he had transformed himself into one of the hardest-working young players in the country. Coaches admired his discipline, while teammates quickly realized that he approached every practice with an intensity that set him apart.Only a few years after finishing a summer without scoring a single point, Bryant had become one of the top high school prospects in America.Kobe Bryant's rise did not happen because everything suddenly became easy. It happened because he refused to let one disappointing summer define his future.At Lower Merion, his reputation continued to grow. He spent extra hours in the gym, challenged older players and treated every practice as another opportunity to improve. Former NBA player Tim Thomas later remembered seeing that competitive mindset during the McDonald's All-American Game.Thomas recalled, "His approach was completely different. We were going through the drills and everyone else is walking through it. He was going full throttle, dunking the ball. We all kind of knew at that moment, this guy is different."That positive attitude helped Bryant become one of the nation's best high school players before entering the 1996 NBA Draft. Selected with the 13th overall pick by the Charlotte Hornets and immediately traded to the Los Angeles Lakers, he began a career that would redefine excellence in basketball.Even after reaching the NBA, Bryant never stopped chasing improvement. Stories of his early morning workouts and late-night practice sessions became legendary. While fans celebrated his performances on game night, Bryant believed the real work happened when nobody was watching.Reflecting on the mindset that drove him throughout his career, Bryant once said, "Everything negative, pressure, challenges, is all an opportunity for me to rise."That philosophy eventually became known around the world as the Mamba Mentality. It was not simply about winning championships or scoring points. It was about embracing difficult moments instead of avoiding them and believing that every setback could become an opportunity to grow.Bryant lived by that belief throughout his career. He won five NBA championships with the Lakers, earned 18 All-Star selections, captured the league's MVP award in 2008 and added two Olympic gold medals with Team USA.Yet even after achieving everything he had dreamed of as a child, he continued searching for ways to improve.He once explained, "The most important thing is to try and inspire people so that they can be great in whatever they want to do."His father's words never promised future championships or NBA stardom. They simply reminded a disappointed boy that love was not measured by points on a scoreboard.That moment gave Bryant the confidence to keep believing in himself when the results suggested otherwise. Everything that followed, from the championships to the Hall of Fame career and the Mamba Mentality that inspired millions, began with a lesson that had nothing to do with basketball itself.Sometimes the biggest turning point in a career is not a trophy or a championship. Sometimes it is a difficult day, and the decision to keep going when giving up feels much easier.
Article Summary: A young Kobe Bryant's scoreless summer league became the turning point that fueled his relentless work ethic and eventually shaped the legendary Mamba Mentality. For a teenager who dreamed of following his father's path to the NBA, the experience was heartbreaking. For many athletes, an experience like that would have been enough to walk away from the sport.

Article Title: “How dumb you have to be”: WNBA gets heavily trolled after futile attempt to delete Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers’ betting video from their official page
Article Text:
Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers. Image via: Getty Images

WNBA deleted Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers' betting video after backlash

Fans troll WNBA's huge blunder

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers clashed on court during Wings vs Dream showdown

The WNBA's own account is the reason Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers are facing gambling questions this week. During All-Star Weekend, the two stars made a friendly $400 bet on which of their teams would win Wednesday's Wings-Dream game, and the league's social media team filmed and posted it, quoting Bueckers on the terms of the wager.The post ran straight into the WNBA's own rulebook. Section 5(c) of the CBA prohibits players from wagering money or anything of value on the outcome of league games, and the clip showed cash changing hands on camera. The league pulled the video within hours, but by then it had already been screenshotted and recirculated widely.The backlash centered on a simple problem: the league's own staff had broadcast conduct that its own agreement forbids. Fans didn't need to dig for the CBA language once people started pointing it out, and the quiet deletion only made the clip more visible.That leaves commissioner Cathy Engelbert with an awkward choice. Disciplining two of the league's most marketable young players over content her own team promoted risks looking heavy-handed. Ignoring it risks signaling the rulebook only applies when convenient. Either way, the original misstep sits with the league office, not the players who agreed to a $400 bet on camera.The reaction online was immediate and unsparing. Fox Sports host Clay Travis wrote:@ClayTravis shared: "I can’t even comprehend how dumb you have to be to post this video from the league’s official account. Like sub 70 IQ. And how stupid are the players too?! On video bets with cash being shown?"Others zeroed in on the enforcement gap. One user, @krk73, wrote:"Endorsing? Pardon....They aren't endorsing players betting on games. The players are literally betting on games on camera."Another, @SachaVeldhuis, predicted nothing would come of it:"So thats a fine or suspension. But nothing wil happen, all jokes. How dumb is this league. Players getting threats from sports bettors. Tonedeaf league."Several fans also raised double-standard questions, asking whether Fever players would have faced faster discipline for the same clip.Wednesday's game gave the story a second act. In the first quarter at College Park Center, Bueckers switched onto Reese in the post. Reese drove at the smaller Bueckers, who forced a turnover and drew a foul in the process, then celebrated the stop by clapping directly at Reese. Reese approached her, words were exchanged, and no technical foul was called on either player. Dallas carried a 38-32 lead into halftime.The two are reportedly friendly away from the court, having spent time together during All-Star Weekend just days earlier. Reese has drawn attention for in-game needling before, and Bueckers isn't a stranger to it either. Whether the league addresses the wager before their next meeting remains the open question hanging over both teams.
Article Summary: Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers made a $400 bet on which of their teams would win Wednesday's Wings-Dream game. The league's social media team filmed and posted it, quoting Buecker on the terms of the wager. The post ran straight into the WNBA's own rulebook. Section 5(c) of the CBA prohibits players from wagering money or anything of value on the outcome of league games.

Article Title: Lamine Yamal's net worth at 19 reveals how far he has come from a childhood of struggle and poverty
Article Text:
Lamine Yamal's struggle and net worth (Getty Images)

What is Lamine Yamal's net worth right now?

How much does Lamine Yamal earn from sponsorships and brand deals?

Where did Lamine Yamal grow up and how did his family get to Spain?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lamine Yamal is 19, a World Cup winner, and sitting on an estimated net worth of something many can only dream of in their lifetime. That figure is only going to grow. In May 2025, Barcelona handed him a six-year contract worth $18 million annually before tax, a deal that landed him tenth on Forbes' list of football's highest earners. The same boy who once slept in an apartment where the bedroom and kitchen shared the same four walls is now one of the most commercially valuable teenagers the sport has ever produced.Celebrity Net Worth puts Lamine Yamal's current wealth at around $15 million, though that number already feels dated. His previous Barcelona contract paid him roughly $1.82 million per year. The club scrapped it. The new deal, signed in the summer of 2025, pays $18 million annually before tax, and that base figure rises further depending on performance bonuses and trophies collected along the way.Barcelona knew exactly what they were protecting. Yamal became the youngest player in the club's history to feature for the first team, doing so at 15 years, nine months, and 16 days. He is the youngest scorer ever for the Spanish national team, the youngest goalscorer in European Championship history, and at 17, the youngest player ever nominated for the Ballon d'Or. Those records are not decorative. They explain why Barcelona moved so fast to lock him down on a long-term deal.His salary is the headline, but the sponsorship income is where the real scale of Lamine Yamal's commercial reach becomes clear. His deal with Adidas is worth approximately $34 million over ten years, making it the anchor of a portfolio that also includes Beats by Dre, OPPO, Powerade, Konami, and UNICEF. For a teenager who has not yet hit his physical peak, that level of brand interest says something about how the market views his trajectory.Most players spend years building that kind of commercial profile. Yamal had it before he turned 18. Brands are not betting on who he is right now. They are betting on who he is going to be for the next decade, and so far, nothing in his career has given them a reason to doubt that investment.Lamine Yamal was born on July 13, 2007, in the Rocafonda neighbourhood of Mataró. His father, Mounir Nasraoui, worked as a building painter of Moroccan origin. His mother, Sheila Ebana, was a waitress from Equatorial Guinea. They separated when Lamine was three. The family lived modestly, in a small apartment where, as Yamal has since admitted, the kitchen and bedroom occupied the same space.The person who shaped him most was his grandmother, Fatima. She arrived in Spain from Morocco with nothing and built everything from scratch. Yamal spoke about it plainly during an appearance on the podcast Resonancia de Corazón con José Ramón de la Morena: "The first to arrive in Spain was my grandmother, who sneaked onto a bus coming from Morocco and managed to reach Mataró."He continued: "She started working 3 jobs so that my father could come, because he stayed in Morocco. And when my grandmother had saved some money, she paid a woman to bring my father and his sister, who came to Spain when they were three years old."That story of sacrifice, grinding and unglamorous, is what sits beneath all the contracts and endorsement deals. Yamal has been open about the fact that providing a more stable life for his family is the part of his success that means the most to him. The money matters. But it matters because of where it came from.
Article Summary: Lamine Yamal is one of the most commercially valuable teenagers in football. The 19-year-old has signed a six-year contract with Barcelona worth $18 million per year. His sponsorship deal with Adidas is worth approximately $34 million over ten years. His family came to Spain from Morocco when he was three.

Article Title: "Not all details from the accident are being shared": Kyle Shanahan car crash mystery deepens as police refuse to release key details after two weeks of silence
Article Text:
kyle shanahan (Getty Images)

Why are officials not revealing more about Kyle Shanahan's car accident?

Kyle Shanahan's absence has become one of the biggest storylines as the San Francisco 49ers opened training camp, but not because of football. The head coach is recovering from serious injuries suffered in a car crash earlier this month, leaving the organisation without its leader during an important stage of pre-season preparations. While the team has disclosed the extent of Shanahan's injuries, several details surrounding the accident remain undisclosed, adding fresh questions as the 49ers balance optimism over his recovery with uncertainty over when he can fully return.The 49ers confirmed that the accident took place on July 14, 2026, near Shanahan's home in Los Altos Hills, California. The collision happened at a busy intersection near Alma Street and Hamilton Avenue on the western edge of downtown Palo Alto, where emergency crews responded after a black Tesla and a blue Mercedes SUV crashed.Shanahan suffered extensive injuries. He sustained a concussion, broke his nose, hand and three ribs, and required 40 stitches to his face. The team also revealed that he continues to experience concussion-like symptoms, preventing him from taking part in training camp for now.Even with those medical updates, much about the crash remains unclear.San Francisco Chronicle reporter Eric Branch highlighted the limited information available, writing: “Kyle Shanahan badly injured in car crash and has ongoing concussion symptoms as camp begins.Not all details from the accident are being shared. ‘There will be no information released regarding the cause of the collision or who was at fault.'”That statement came from Lt. Nicholas Martinez, who confirmed that both drivers remained at the scene and fully cooperated with investigators. Authorities also said no citations were issued and there was no indication that either driver was impaired.General manager John Lynch acknowledged that Shanahan is still focused on his recovery rather than football.“He’s not ready yet to be talking to you guys. The 49ers battled through a string of injuries during the 2025 season yet remained competitive and kept themselves in the playoff conversation. Entering a new campaign with high expectations, the organisation will want stability from the outset.Shanahan's role stretches far beyond calling plays. He shapes the team's identity, oversees day-to-day operations and remains central to every major football decision. While training camp continues under the coaching staff, the focus will stay firmly on his health until he is cleared to resume full duties.
Article Summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan suffered serious injuries in a car crash earlier this month. He sustained a concussion, broke his nose, hand and three ribs, and required 40 stitches to his face.
