Article Title: Why was Isaiah Rider arrested? Former Lakers star is in police custody in a case related to his wife Vanessa
Article Text:
Isaiah Rider. Image via: Getty Images

Former NBA champion Isaiah Rider arrested, again

What happened to Isaiah Rider?

Is Isaiah Rider's latest arrest related to his wife Vanessa?

Isaiah Rider was arrested again Thursday night, his third arrest in less than two months, this time on a misdemeanor charge for failing to comply with a court order. Maricopa County jail records show the former NBA Slam Dunk champion was booked Friday morning, pleaded guilty, and is expected to remain in custody until Tuesday.The charge traces back to a protective order his estranged wife, Vanessa, obtained last year. Rider, 55, has now been arrested twice before in connection with that same order, and the latest booking keeps a messy divorce and custody dispute firmly in public view.This is not new territory for Rider. He was picked up twice in December, first for allegedly violating the protective order and then again days later for skipping a hearing on whether that order should stay in place.A judge extended it after Vanessa showed up and Rider did not.Thursday's arrest follows the same pattern, a court-related misdemeanor rather than a new allegation of contact or violence, per TMZ . Police records describe it simply as a failure to comply with a court order, and the guilty finding suggests Rider did not contest it once he was in front of a judge.The former fifth overall pick in the 1993 NBA Draft spent nine seasons in the league, three years apiece with the Minnesota Timberwolves and Portland Trail Blazers before single seasons with the Atlanta Hawks, Los Angeles Lakers and Denver Nuggets.He won the Slam Dunk Contest as a rookie in 1994 and picked up a championship ring in 2001, even though he did not make the Lakers' playoff roster that year.The trouble began last year when Vanessa filed for a protective order, alleging Rider had been hostile toward her on multiple occasions. Court documents describe threatening language directed at her and their teenage son. Rider has denied the allegations and pointed instead to the timing of his own divorce filing in November 2024, arguing the order followed shortly after he moved to end the marriage.The order barred Rider from contacting Vanessa or their son and from going near the family home or the boy's school. Rider has claimed in filings that he did not receive the paperwork until December, weeks after it was granted in July.He was arrested that same month for allegedly violating the order, then arrested again for missing the hearing on whether it should be extended. Vanessa appeared for that hearing. The judge sided with her and kept the order in place, setting up the conditions that led to Thursday's arrest.Yes, at least indirectly. Thursday's booking was not for a new incident involving Vanessa but for failing to comply with a court order that exists because of her original petition, which makes this arrest part of the same unresolved case rather than a separate legal matter.Vanessa has been consistent about her reasons for seeking the order in the first place. "The Order of Protection was sought and granted solely for safety reasons, to protect myself and my child from further harm," she said in a statement , adding that she views the process as necessary rather than tactical and has asked the public to respect the privacy of a case involving a minor.
Article Summary: Isaiah Rider was arrested again Thursday night, this time on a misdemeanor charge for failing to comply with a court order. The charge traces back to a protective order his estranged wife, Vanessa, obtained last year. Rider, 55, has now been arrested twice before in connection with that same order.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible. They give me peace of mind” - How Rafael Nadal’s fam
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible. They give me peace of mind” - How Rafael Nadal’s family stood by him through every injury on his road to tennis immortality (Image via Getty)

How did Rafael Nadal overcome a career-threatening foot condition?

Why did Rafael Nadal always choose family and home over fame?

What did Rafael Nadal say about his wife and family during his injury battles?

What life lesson did Rafael Nadal learn from pain and defeat?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For years, Rafael Nadal inspired fans with his fight on the tennis court. What many people did not see was the battle he fought away from the spotlight. Long before becoming a 22-time Grand Slam champion, Nadal was told that a rare foot condition could end his career. He dealt with constant pain, serious injuries and doubts about whether he could keep playing. Yet he kept coming back. While his determination made headlines, Nadal has always said his biggest strength was the people who stood beside him. Their support helped him survive the hardest moments and build one of the greatest careers in tennis history.In 2005, Rafael Nadal won his first French Open title at just 19 years old. Soon after that breakthrough, he was diagnosed with Mueller-Weiss syndrome, a rare condition that affects the bones in the foot. Doctors warned that continuing his career at the highest level might not be possible.Instead of giving up, Nadal returned home to Manacor in Mallorca. There, he was surrounded by his father Sebastián, mother Ana María, sister Maribel and his longtime partner Mery Perelló. Their support gave him the strength to keep moving forward when his future looked uncertain.Looking back on those difficult years, Nadal once said:“Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible. They give me peace of mind.”Despite becoming one of the biggest names in world sport, Nadal never left the place where he grew up. He stayed close to his family in Manacor and continued living the simple life that had shaped him from childhood.His uncle and longtime coach Toni Nadal taught him to stay humble, respect opponents and never believe he was bigger than the game. Those lessons stayed with him throughout his career.Rafael Nadal has often explained that returning home helped him switch off from the pressure of professional tennis. In Manacor, he was simply Rafa, spending time with friends and family. That normal life became an important part of maintaining his mental balance through the highs and lows of the sport.Nadal’s wife, Mery “Xisca” Perelló, was by his side long before he became a global star. She witnessed every comeback, every rehabilitation session and every painful setback that fans rarely saw.As injuries continued in the final years of his career, those shared sacrifices became even more meaningful. With his wife, young son and team watching from the stands, Nadal reflected on everything they had gone through together.He said:“Having my family here, my wife, my son, my team… it’s emotional because they know how hard the process has been. They have been through the good moments, but especially the tough moments during all these years of injuries.”Nadal never believed success came without suffering. Throughout his career, he played through injuries, long matches and physical pain that would have stopped many athletes. Instead of running from those challenges, he accepted them as part of the journey.That mindset became one of the biggest reasons behind his remarkable career.As Nadal explained:“If you don’t lose, you cannot enjoy the victories. You have to accept both things. I learned during my career to enjoy suffering.”His story goes far beyond Grand Slam trophies or records. It shows that true strength is not only about winning titles but also about staying grounded when life becomes difficult. Through every injury and every comeback, Nadal never lost sight of the people who mattered most. Their love gave him the peace, confidence and support to keep chasing his dreams, making his journey one of the most inspiring stories in modern sport.
Article Summary: Rafael Nadal was diagnosed with a rare foot condition at just 19 years old. Doctors told him it could end his career, but he refused to give up. Nadal returned home to Manacor in Mallorca to be with his family. He said: “Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family,Without my team, it would be impossible. They give me peace of mind”

Article Title: Delhi-NCR commuters may be losing a whole day of week to commuting
Article Text:

Expertspeak





NEW DELHI: Every weekday at 5am, Manish (31) leaves his home in Bahadurgarh for a twohour commute to Vikas Bhawan. His journey involves a motorcycle ride to the Delhi border, a bus to Madhuban Chowk, the metro to ITO and a final walk.For the past seven years, he has followed the same routine, returning home close to 8pm.“Everything costs more here. If I move closer to Delhi, I’ll save time but lose money to rent and expensive schools. Sometimes, the journey seems longer than the day itself. But that’s the compromise I make so my family doesn’t have to,” he says.Manish is, of course, not alone. TOI looks at travel travails of a few others.At 6.45am every weekday, 25-year-old Aashita’s alarm goes off. An hour later, she leaves her home in Faridabad for a nearly two-hour commute to her office in Delhi.By the time she returns, almost four hours have been spent on the road. For months, she relied on the metro. But multiple interchanges and overcrowded trains made the daily routine exhausting. “Sometimes, four or five trains pass before I can even get in. Most days, you’re standing the entire way,” she says.A few weeks ago, she switched to carpooling. “It’s definitely more comfortable, but not much faster because of Delhi traffic,” she says.People often ask why she doesn’t move closer to work. “I recently got married and live with my husband’s family in Faridabad. Shifting isn’t really an option,” she says.Aman is driven by economics. While much of Hapur is still waking up, 25-year-old Aman is already driving to Noida. The Delhi-Meerut Expressway has made the journey smoother, not shorter. He chose to stay with his family in Hapur instead of renting a flat in Noida to save money.“Financially, it made sense, but the real cost is time,” he says. “By the time I get home, I’m too tired to do anything except have dinner and sleep,” he says. Even weekends don’t always offer a break. “No matter how much I want to meet my friends, it feels tiring to travel to Delhi again when my entire week has already been spent commuting,” he says. “If you save on rent, you end up sacrificing your own time.”For Sukriti, marriage added two hours to every working day. After moving to Gurgaon, where her husband works, her daily commute to Noida has doubled to almost four hours. “My husband leaves in the morning while I leave in the evening. By the time I return after sunrise, he’s getting ready for work. We barely see each other,” she says. “You don’t realise how quickly four hours disappear every day until you live that routine. We had to think about both our jobs. Mine is hybrid, but his is full-time, so living in Gurgaon made more sense.”Dr Sameer Malhotra, principal director and head, department of mental health and behavioural sciences, Max Healthcare, Saket and Panchsheel Park, says, “In a region like NCR, time poverty is almost inevitable. Whether people travel by metro or car,the real stress isn’t the distance but the unpredictability—traffic jams, honking, pollution and the constant uncertainty of reaching on time. Over time, this can lead to emotional burnout, along with physical problems. The bigger loss is the time people no longer have for family, friends or hobbies. AI-enabled trafficmanagement, flexible work models and workplaces closer to where employees live can help ease this burden.”Different lives, different reasons, but the compromise is the same: every weekday, hours that could have been spent with family, friends or simply resting are instead lost to the commute.
Article Summary: Every weekday at 5am, Manish leaves his home in Bahadurgarh for a two-hour commute to Vikas Bhawan. For Sukriti, marriage added two hours to every working day. Aman chose to stay with his family in Hapur instead of renting a flat in Noida to save money.

Article Title: 'Should’ve come after warnings, discussions': Mumbai restaurants after FDA suspends licenses
Article Text:
Some, like the Parsi Dairy Farm in Marine Lines, reopened only on Tuesday after another round of inspection was carried out by the area’s food safety team.





MUMBAI:Following back-to-back inspection of food establishments by the FDA, which has been on a licence suspension spree across the city’s restaurant landscape, eateries are finding themselves racing to fix violations and file appeals within 15 days in order to reopen.Many of their workers have been sent back to their villages as business remains shut.There are about 82 appeal applications across the state so far, with half of them originating in the city.Assistant commissioner (food) Santosh Kamble said that after paperwork is submitted, an FDA team conducts a physical verification.“If the compliance is not as required, we ask them to rectify the remaining issues and then allot them a revised date,” he said.Some, like the Parsi Dairy Farm in Marine Lines, reopened only on Tuesday after another round of inspection was carried out by the area’s food safety team.The outlet had faced issues like fungal growth on walls, the storage of raw materials directly on the floor, and pest and rodent infestations. A representative said compliance reports have been submitted regarding all violations and that fixes have been made.Bristol Bakery in Mahim, a sister outlet of Jimmy Boy, reopened on Wednesday after days of renovation work.A person closely associated with the outlet said they have addressed structural issues such as broken tiles, and pest control has been conducted again.The person said that at the time of the inspection, issues such as flour on the floor were pointed out without considering that it is bound to happen around machinery.“All of the inspections are a positive move on the part of the FDA. We only wish they had held talks with us first, because this is very sudden. Most of us conduct monthly repairs and checks, with major repairs done annually.For years, there was very limited interaction, and now suddenly they are in full force,” the person said.FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe said that in the early days after he took over, meetings were held with the Indian Hotel & Restaurant Association and similar organisations.“We provided them with all the instructions. They are well aware that certain standards need to be implemented, which have been in force since 2011,” he said.Bhendi Bazaar’s Shalimar restaurant still remains shut a week after its suspension, undergoing extensive renovation work.Its neighbour, Noor Mohammadi, remains closed, but one of its representatives said the kitchen is getting a complete makeover.“We wish they had given us a notice. We have already filed an appeal and have told them we will take some time,” he said.
Article Summary: There are about 82 appeal applications across the state so far, with half of them originating in the city. Some, like the Parsi Dairy Farm in Marine Lines, reopened only on Tuesday after another round of inspection was carried out by the area’s food safety team.

Article Title: 80-year-old farmer injured in leopard attack, forest dept installs cages
Article Text:
Kolhapur:





An 80-year-old farmer from Majle village in Hatkanangale tehsil of Kolhapur district got injured in a leopard attack on Tuesday evening, prompting the forest department to begin search operations and installation of cages in the area.A pet dog was also attacked by the leopard late on Tuesday at Atigre village in Hatkanangale tehsil. As per the information received from Karvir range forest department, the injured farmer has been identified as Nemgonda Jingonda Patil.He is a resident of Majle village and had gone to his farm to cut the grass on the embankment. While the farmer was working, a leopard emerged from the nearby bushes and attacked him.Hearing Patil’s call for help the nearby farmers came running to his rescue. Amidst the chaos, the leopard ran inside the sugarcane farm. The villagers took the farmer to a private hospital at Hatkanangale.After receiving information about the attack, a team of the forest department immediately arrived and started a search operation.The forest department has set up cages to trap the leopard. A search operation with the help of a drone was underway on Wednesday by the Rapid Rescue Team of the Kolhapur forest department.Sanjay Kamble, forest ranger of Hatkanangle, said, “The pugmarks are not clear owing to the rain. However, it is more likely that there are multiple leopards in the area. We will continue with the search operation with the help of drones. Cages have also been set up in the village to trap the leopard. The villagers and farmers from Majle and Aalte should remain vigilant.”
Article Summary: An 80-year-old farmer from Majle village in Hatkanangale tehsil of Kolhapur district got injured in a leopard attack on Tuesday evening. The forest department has set up cages to trap the leopard. A search operation with the help of a drone was underway on Wednesday.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:
Khopoli police arrested four burglars for stealing silver items from a historic temple





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.
